title: Implement AgentList sidebar with agent cards
description:
Create src/components/AgentList/AgentList.tsx, src/components/AgentList/AgentList.module.css, src/components/AgentCard/AgentCard.tsx, and src/components/AgentCard/AgentCard.module.css.

## Visual Design Reference
Read these screenshots to match the visual design:
- Read /tmp/loom-frontend-e2e/designs/sidebar.png — full sidebar showing agent list and work queue
- Read /tmp/loom-frontend-e2e/designs/agent-card.png — close-up of a single agent card
- Read /tmp/loom-frontend-e2e/designs/full-page.png — overall page layout for context

Design reference URL (supplementary): https://designs.magicpath.ai/v1/friendly-cliff-4837

The sidebar contains a list of agent cards below an "Agents" header with a count badge. Each agent card shows an avatar circle (colored with the agent's color, white initial letter), the agent name and role, commit count on the right side (green "+N" format), and a status indicator. A small status dot appears on the avatar indicating the agent's current state (working, ready, error, idle).

AgentList props: AgentListProps { agents: Agent[]; onAgentClick?: (agent: Agent) => void; }. Render header "Agents" with count badge, then list of AgentCard components.

AgentCard props: AgentCardProps { agent: Agent; onClick?: () => void; }. Card layout: horizontal row with avatar, info section (name + role), and right-side stats (commit count + status text). Status dot colors: ready=gray, working=yellow/amber, error=red, idle=gray.

Export default function AgentList and export default function AgentCard from their respective files.

title: Create WorkQueue stats panel
description:
Create src/components/WorkQueue/WorkQueue.tsx and src/components/WorkQueue/WorkQueue.module.css.

## Visual Design Reference
Read these screenshots to match the visual design:
- Read /tmp/loom-frontend-e2e/designs/sidebar.png — shows work queue panel below the agent list
- Read /tmp/loom-frontend-e2e/designs/full-page.png — overall layout context

Design reference URL (supplementary): https://designs.magicpath.ai/v1/friendly-cliff-4837

The Work Queue panel sits at the bottom of the sidebar. It has a collapsible header "Work Queue" with a chevron toggle. When expanded, it shows a 2-column grid of status labels and their counts (Backlog, Open, Blocked, In Progress, Needs Review, Done). Below the grid is a summary line showing open/closed counts and completion percentage.

Props: WorkQueueProps { stats: WorkQueueStats; }. Use useState for collapsed/expanded state, default expanded.

Grid layout: 2-column grid with status labels on the left and counts on the right. Status labels: Backlog, Open, Blocked, In Progress, Needs Review, Done — mapped to stats fields.

Below grid: summary line — calculate total = sum of all stats, closed = stats.done, openCount = total - closed, percentage = Math.round(closed/total*100). Render: "{openCount} open - {closed} closed - {percentage}%".

Export default function WorkQueue.

title: Create Agent Detail Panel modal for agent cards
description:
Create src/components/AgentDetailPanel/AgentDetailPanel.tsx and src/components/AgentDetailPanel/AgentDetailPanel.module.css.

## Visual Design Reference
Read these screenshots to match the visual design:
- Read /tmp/loom-frontend-e2e/designs/agent-detail-panel.png — the agent detail modal panel
- Read /tmp/loom-frontend-e2e/designs/full-page.png — overall layout context

Design reference URL (supplementary): https://designs.magicpath.ai/v1/friendly-cliff-4837

This is a slide-in modal panel that opens from the right side when the user clicks an AgentCard. It displays detailed agent information.

Props: AgentDetailPanelProps { agent: Agent; onClose: () => void; }

Layout — Modal with backdrop overlay:
- Backdrop covers the full screen with a semi-transparent dark overlay.
- Panel slides in from the right side, taking up about 420px width and full height, with a white background.

Header section:
- Close button (X) in the top-right corner.
- Agent avatar (larger circle with agent color and white initial letter).
- Agent name prominently displayed next to avatar.
- Status badge pill next to name. If agent.status==="working", show yellow indicator + "Has Changes". If "error", red + "Error". If "ready", green + "Ready".
- Below: worktree path text "webui/{agent.id}".

Tab switcher:
- Two tabs: "Info" and "Logs". Horizontal row with bottom border.
- Active tab has bold text with a bottom border accent. Inactive tab is muted.
- Use useState to track active tab, default "Info".

Info tab contents (sections with uppercase labels):
1. CURRENT TASK: If agent has changes, show "Implementing current task". Otherwise "No active task".
2. COMMIT STATUS: Green badge showing "+{agent.commitCount} ahead". Below: list of 2-3 mock commit messages.
3. CHANGES: Show "M .agent.lock" with M in orange/amber.
4. AGENT INFO: Key-value display with Branch (agent.id) and Status (agent.statusText).

Logs tab: Show "No logs available" centered.

Integration: Parent manages "activeAgent" state. When AgentCard clicked, set activeAgent. Render AgentDetailPanel when activeAgent is set.

Export default function AgentDetailPanel.

title: Initialize React+Vite+TypeScript project scaffold
description:
Initialize the cortex-kanban project as a React 18 + Vite + TypeScript application. Create the following project scaffold files: 1. package.json — name "cortex-kanban", type "module". Dependencies: react ^18, react-dom ^18. Dev dependencies: @types/react, @types/react-dom, @vitejs/plugin-react, typescript ^5, vite ^5, vitest, @testing-library/react, @testing-library/jest-dom, jsdom. Scripts: "dev": "vite", "build": "tsc && vite build", "preview": "vite preview", "test": "vitest run". 2. tsconfig.json — target ES2020, jsx react-jsx, strict mode, module ESNext, moduleResolution bundler, noEmit true, include ["src"]. 3. vite.config.ts — import and use @vitejs/plugin-react. 4. index.html — standard Vite entry point loading /src/main.tsx, title "Cortex Kanban". 5. src/vite-env.d.ts — Vite client types reference. 6. src/main.tsx — import App from ./App and render into #root with React.StrictMode. Import ./index.css for global styles. 7. src/index.css — CSS reset (box-sizing border-box on all elements, body margin/padding 0), body font-family system stack (-apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, Segoe UI, etc.), background #f5f3ee, color #1a1a1a. 8. src/App.tsx — placeholder component: export default function App() returning
Cortex
. 9. src/App.module.css — empty placeholder CSS module file. 10. Create empty directories: src/components, src/data. After creating all files, run npm install and verify the build succeeds (npm run build). The project must compile cleanly with no errors.

title: Set up ESLint and pre-commit quality check script
description:
Set up code quality tooling and a pre-commit check script for the cortex-kanban project.

1. Install ESLint with TypeScript and React support as dev dependencies:
   - eslint
   - @eslint/js
   - typescript-eslint
   - eslint-plugin-react-hooks
   - eslint-plugin-react-refresh

2. Create eslint.config.js using the flat config format:
   - Extend @eslint/js recommended and typescript-eslint recommended
   - Add react-hooks plugin with recommended rules
   - Add react-refresh plugin with warn on non-component exports
   - Set files pattern to ["src/**/*.{ts,tsx}"]
   - Ignore dist/ and node_modules/

3. Add npm scripts:
   - "lint": "eslint src/"
   - "lint:fix": "eslint src/ --fix"
   - "quality-check": "npm run lint && tsc --noEmit && npm test"

4. Create scripts/pre-commit.sh — a shell script that runs the quality-check npm script. It should be executable (chmod +x) and exit non-zero if any check fails. Include a comment explaining it can be symlinked as .git/hooks/pre-commit.

5. Verify all existing source code passes the lint check (npm run lint should exit 0). Fix any lint errors found in existing code.

Do NOT set up husky or modify .git/hooks directly — just provide the standalone script.

title: Create Playwright visual tests for the rendered app
description:
Set up Playwright end-to-end visual tests for the cortex-kanban application.

1. Install @playwright/test as a dev dependency.

2. Create playwright.config.ts:
   - Use chromium only (projects: [{ name: "chromium", use: { ...devices["Desktop Chrome"] } }])
   - Set webServer to run "npm run preview" on port 4173 (Vite preview default)
   - Set baseURL to http://localhost:4173
   - Set testDir to "e2e"
   - Set retries to 0
   - Set timeout to 30000

3. Create e2e/app.spec.ts with these test cases:
   a. "renders header with Cortex title" — navigate to /, verify h1 contains "Cortex"
   b. "renders all six kanban columns" — verify column headers: Backlog, Open, Blocked, In Progress, Needs Review, Done
   c. "renders issue cards with priority badges" — verify at least one P0, P1, P2, P3 badge is visible
   d. "renders agent list in sidebar" — verify "Agents" heading and at least 3 agent names (Cobalt, Falcon, Nova) are visible
   e. "renders work queue stats" — verify "Work Queue" heading and stat labels (Backlog, Open, Blocked) are visible
   f. "search filters issue cards" — type "database" in the search input, verify the URGENT database issue is visible and the WebSocket issue is not
   g. "full page screenshot" — take a full-page screenshot saved to e2e/screenshots/full-page.png

4. Add npm scripts:
   - "test:e2e": "playwright test"
   - "test:e2e:headed": "playwright test --headed"

5. Add e2e/screenshots/ to .gitignore (or create .gitignore if it does not exist).

6. Run npx playwright install chromium to install the browser binary, then verify all tests pass with npm run test:e2e.

Important: build the app first (npm run build) before running visual tests, since Vite preview serves from dist/.

title: Create Task Detail Panel modal for issue cards
description:
Create src/components/TaskDetailPanel/TaskDetailPanel.tsx and src/components/TaskDetailPanel/TaskDetailPanel.module.css.

## Visual Design Reference
Read these screenshots to match the visual design:
- Read /tmp/loom-frontend-e2e/designs/task-detail-panel.png — the task detail modal
- Read /tmp/loom-frontend-e2e/designs/full-page.png — overall layout context

Design reference URL (supplementary): https://designs.magicpath.ai/v1/friendly-cliff-4837

This is a centered modal that opens when the user clicks an IssueCard. It displays detailed task/issue information.

Props: TaskDetailPanelProps { issue: Issue; onClose: () => void; blockedByIssues?: Issue[]; }

Layout — Centered modal with backdrop overlay:
- Backdrop covers full screen with semi-transparent dark overlay.
- Panel is centered, approximately 640px wide, with rounded corners and white background. Max height limited with vertical scroll.

Header row:
- Issue ID in monospace.
- Priority badge (same colors as IssueCard: P0=red, P1=orange, P2=amber, P3=blue, P4=gray with white text).
- Status badge: uppercase text with colored background (backlog=gray, open=green, blocked=red, in_progress=amber, review=blue, done=muted gray).
- Close button (X) right-aligned.

Title: Large bold text below the header row.

Assignee + Owner row (two columns):
- ASSIGNEE (uppercase label): If issue.assignedAgent, show agent avatar + name + status. Otherwise show placeholder avatar + "Unassigned" + "No status set".
- OWNER (uppercase label): Show "tysonthomas9@noreply.github.com" (hardcoded mock).

DESCRIPTION section (uppercase label):
- Show a paragraph of descriptive text. Use a generic placeholder: "Task description will appear here when provided."

BLOCKED BY section (only if blockedByIssues has items):
- Label: "BLOCKED BY ({count})".
- Each blocker: styled row with red/pink background, lock icon, blocker issue ID badge, and blocker title.

DESIGN section:
- Collapsible "Summary" accordion with chevron toggle. Content: mock design text "Implementation plan will appear here after planning phase."

ACTIVITY section:
- "No comments yet" placeholder.
- Comment textarea input and "Post Comment" button (green).

Click backdrop or press Escape to close.

Integration: Parent manages "selectedIssue" state. When IssueCard clicked, set selectedIssue. Render TaskDetailPanel when selectedIssue is set. For blockedByIssues, filter issues to find blockers for "blocked" status issues.

Export default function TaskDetailPanel.
